text: The buy-back writes one `listing` row and one `asset_sale` row in `rwb_asset`; the case move is answered to rwb-case, the deviation is raised on the rwb-deviation contract, the signature is the approval child workflow of the kit on rwb-decision with its limit as a delegated-authority row of rwb-access read at its version, and the template price is read from rwb-comms and lands in `floor_price` or `sale_price` as the tagged contract baseline decides.
why: Legacy RWB-E4-032 publishes no buy-back operation, gives no limit value and no template-price field, and LOV-SALE-CHANNEL and LOV-LISTING hold no buy-back value; without a default the application story could not start on Day 1.
read: Legacy story RWB-E4-032 Story, AC1 to AC3, Data, Endpoints and Validation and messages; FSD S5 A2.23; TSD S5 T3.1, T3.2, T6.1, T-A; rule rows R-DIS-24, R-DIS-61, R-DIS-62, R-DIS-66; context pack S5.
confirm: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the P7 rwb-decision owner and the P4 rwb-access owner at the baseline review
impact: The story fixes the rows and the call set now; the limit value, the template-price column and the two list values can change as reference and contract data without a change to any business criterion.

text: The buy-back element of the two reads carries the listing and asset_sale columns of TSD S5 T3.1 and the four closed lists of T3.2 unchanged; the case-move answer, the deviation raise, the approval child and the template read are declared with the placeholder of R9 and a 2 s timeout; the decision-record element is the platform library's; and the baseline is tagged before the application story builds.
why: Four of the five consumed rows have no published name or shape in any source, the approval answer and the deviation reference have no element, and the two lists have no buy-back value; the contract story must still be finishable and taggable on Day 1.
read: FSD S5 A2.23; TSD S5 T3.1, T3.2, T6.1, T-A.1, T-A.2; rule rows R-DIS-24 and R-DIS-66; context pack S5 naming rules; split plan patterns and empty C list.
confirm: Solution architect of S5 with the S8, P7 and P6 contract owners at the baseline review
impact: Consumers build against fakes on Day 1; each placeholder is replaced by a published name when its owner publishes it, with no change to the element's own fields.

text: The buy-back step starts from ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER, the from state of R-DIS-24, and legacy AC1 is read with that state although the criterion names none; the refusal of R-DIS-27 stays with the route-approval slice, and R-DIS-24 governs the feature although the FSD rule list of A2.23 omits it.
why: AC1 gives no from state, the rule set and the TSD state table give ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER, and the FSD rule list of the feature leaves out the rule the criterion turns on.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-032 AC1 and AC2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DIS-24, R-DIS-27 and R-DIS-66; TSD S5 T4; FSD S5 A2.23.3.1.
confirm: P3 rwb-case owner with the business analyst of module S5 at the baseline review
impact: The criterion text is unchanged; only the state the step is entered from is fixed, and the refusal path stays outside this slice.

text: The signature that R-DIS-24 requires is the approval child workflow of the workflow kit on rwb-decision, and the limit it applies is a delegated-authority row of rwb-access read at its version; rwb-asset holds no limit value and makes no authority decision of its own.
why: No source gives a limit value, the delegated-authority table is not read by this work package and belongs to rwb-access, and the FSD makes the approval a condition of the feature rather than a computation of the service.
read: Rule row R-DIS-24; FSD S5 A2.23.1 and A2.23.3.1; Temporal and Drools Design slide 12 (Approval (DoA) and where S1 to S9 use the kit); context pack S5.
confirm: P7 rwb-decision owner with the P4 rwb-access owner at the baseline review
impact: The step waits on an approval answer and writes nothing until it is approved; the limit can change as a data row without a code change.

text: The customer (borrower) named as an also-user by the FSD is a party of the case and not a Workbench user: no right is granted to it in this slice, and any customer-facing signature or view belongs to the partner gateway and rwb-partner (S9).
why: The rights matrix of the service has no customer role and the legacy permission checks name Workbench roles only.
read: FSD S5 A2.23.3.3; TSD S5 T6.1; legacy RWB-E4-032 Permission checks table.
confirm: P4 rwb-access owner with the S9 rwb-partner owner before the portal work starts
impact: No right and no screen for a customer in this slice; the element carries the party key only.

text: Both stories carry Status Draft (realignment v1) and proceed without a human approval of any source document or of the contract baseline, as D-RCV-60 allows.
why: The run has no human approval step, the sources of the two stories are not signed off, and AGENTS.md rules 9 and 10 record a missing approval as an assumption and let the work continue in Draft.
read: Template and Rules v1 R8.1; AGENTS.md rules 9 and 10; the document control of the sources read by this work package.
applied_in: Metadata row Status of RWB-S5-E4032-APP and RWB-S5-E4032-CON; change log of both stories
